native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: The highest growth phase between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE occurred in the 15th century BCE (c. 1500–1401 BCE), with the strongest extension into the 14th century BCE (sustained growth phase 15th–14th c. BCE). This is based on the growth rate of the 100-year smoothed human-induced landscape openness score (pollen_grate_100, treated as a demographic indicator): the 15th c. BCE has the highest mean (0.00193/yr) and maximum (0.00465) growth rate and the largest share of positive-growth years (80%), confirmed independently by the KDE growth rate of archaeological data (g_all_mean, 0.00284/yr in the 15th c. vs 0.00142 in the 14th). Peak annual growth rates cluster around 1415–1430 BCE. Consistency check: the smoothed openness level (pollen_inter_100) is at its window-low in the 15th c. and reaches its maximum only later (~1241 BCE, 13th c.), as expected when a level lags its growth rate — the 15th–14th c. BCE growth phase is what drives the subsequent openness peak. If 'highest growth phase' is read as the peak of the smoothed openness level rather than the growth rate, the answer would instead be the 13th c. BCE; under the study's growth-rate definition, the 15th c. BCE (with the 14th c. BCE as the adjacent strong century) is the answer.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE −4100…−500; calBP = 1950+|CE|) and isolated the 901 rows for CE −2000…−1100 (2000–1100 BCE). 2) Binned into the nine centuries (20th–12th c. BCE) and computed per-century mean and max of pollen_grate_100 (growth rate of 100-yr smoothed openness) and g_all_mean (KDE growth rate), plus mean level of pollen_inter_100. Table: 20th c.: mean grate −0.00087 / gall 0.00007; 19th: 0.00018 / 0.00028; 18th: −0.00028 / −0.00008; 17th: 0.00087 / 0.00005; 16th: −0.00302 / 0.00117; 15th: 0.00193 / 0.00284; 14th: 0.00111 / 0.00142; 13th: −0.00020 / −0.00158; 12th: −0.00105 / −0.00440. 3) Ranked centuries: 15th c. BCE is #1 by both growth measures (1.7× the 2nd-place 14th c. by pollen_grate_100); no tie — the 15th and 14th c. BCE are the only adjacent strongly-positive pair, reported as the sustained-growth reading. 4) Cross-checked the level: pollen_inter_100 minimum in the 15th c. (0.365), maximum ~1241 BCE (13th c., 2.232), confirming the growth-rate peak precedes the level peak. 5) Located annual peaks: top growth years CE −1415…−1428 (~1415–1430 BCE).
